skill.name: browser-extension-developer
skill.description: Use this skill when developing or maintaining browser extension code in the `browser/` directory, including Chrome/Firefox/Edge compatibility, content scripts, background scripts, or i18n updates.
skill.body:
# Browser Extension Developer

Cross-browser extension (Chrome/Firefox/Edge) using **WXT framework** with Manifest V3. Injects "Repomix" button into GitHub repository pages.

## Structure

```plaintext
browser/
├── entrypoints/       # background.ts, content.ts
├── public/_locales/   # i18n (12 languages)
├── wxt.config.ts      # WXT configuration
└── .output/           # Built files (chrome-mv3, firefox-mv2)
```

## Commands

- `npm run dev` - Development mode (Chrome default)
- `npm run dev:firefox` - Firefox dev mode
- `npm run build-all` - Build all browsers
- `npm run lint` / `npm run test`

## i18n

12 languages: en, ja, de, fr, es, pt_BR, id, vi, ko, zh_CN, zh_TW, hi

New language: Create `public/_locales/[code]/messages.json` with keys: appDescription, openWithRepomix

## Notes

- Chrome/Edge use `chrome.*` APIs, Firefox may need polyfills
- Run lint and tests before completion

generated_query: I need to add Hindi language support to the Repomix browser extension. I've already created a folder `browser/public/_locales/hi/` and a `messages.json` file with the keys `appDescription` and `openWithRepomix` translated. But when I switch my browser language to Hindi, the extension still shows English text. It works fine for other languages like Japanese. Also, after my changes, the extension stopped working entirely on Firefox – it loads in Chrome but not in Firefox. Can you check the `wxt.config.ts` to make sure the new locale is registered, verify the content script and background script still work across Chrome and Firefox, and fix any API compatibility issues? After that, run the linter and tests to confirm everything is clean.

edit_instructions.target_text: New language: Create `public/_locales/[code]/messages.json` with keys: appDescription, openWithRepomix
edit_instructions.rationale: Deleting the instruction for adding a new locale means the skill no longer guides the user on how to properly add Hindi, leaving the registration step unspecified and failing the core task.
